This is a real Claude Code session, sped up where it's marked.
A teacher types one sentence. Make a projectile motion lab where students predict the launch angle to hit a target, auto-graded, with the target distance set by the teacher.
Claude reads the template's guides and plans the lab. That part took about two minutes.
Then it writes the student page, the SpeedGrader view, and the settings.
When it's done, it explains what it built and the choices it made, so the teacher can check them.
A security check reviews the files.
Next, the teacher types zest build. It checks the package for anything Canvas would break, and packages it.
It passed. About three minutes, from one sentence to a file that's ready to upload.
Now the result, in our stand-in Canvas.
The teacher opens Zest from the Canvas editor and uploads the file. Zest shows the lab's settings. The teacher keeps the defaults and embeds it.
A student opens the assignment. First try: thirty degrees. It lands about ten meters past the target.
Second try: twenty-two point four degrees. A hit.
The student submits, and the score goes to the gradebook.
Eight out of ten, graded automatically. The teacher never wrote a line of code.
